name: goblin

attributes.attribute: general name for an evil fairy
mischievous at best and dangerous at worst
rooted in the Celtic vision of the Otherworld
distinct from gnomes, which come from alchemy

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A goblin is a general name for an evil fairy. This British folkloric figure can be mischievous and irritating. At worst it is dangerous. Goblins appeared in many forms. These include the vough, the pooka, and the bogie. The water horse also counts as a goblin. All share roots in the Celtic Otherworld. They differ from gnomes, which come from alchemy. Christina Rossetti used fairy lore in her poem Goblin Market. The poem links evil goblins with fairy kidnapping.

okr.objective: Define the goblin as an evil fairy of British folklore rooted in the Celtic Otherworld.
